```{r load-library-depth-data}
read_counts_df <- readxl::read_xlsx(path = p.library_size_file) %>% 
  pivot_longer(where(is.numeric),
               names_to = "norm_type",
               values_to = "seq_library_size") %>%
  mutate(
    library = gsub(pattern = "[[:punct:]]",
                   replacement = '-',
                   x = library)
  ) %>% 
  extract_metadata_from_library_names()
```

```{r define-category-palettes}

metadata_palette_list <- read_counts_df %>% 
  dplyr::distinct(subunit, strain.type, sugar, group) %>% 
  colour_metadata(
    brewer_palette_name = c("BrBG", "Paired", "Set3", "Spectral"),
    palette_size = 11
  )

subunit_pal_names <- setNames(
  unique(pull(read_counts_df, subunit)),
  c("Blues", "Greens", "Purples", "Reds")
)
metadata_palette_list[["group"]] <- setNames("#969696", c("WT"))
for (i in seq(1, length(subunit_pal_names))) {
  n <- read_counts_df %>%
    filter(
      subunit == subunit_pal_names[[i]],
      group != "WT") %>%
    distinct(group) %>%
    colour_metadata(brewer_palette_name = names(subunit_pal_names)[i])
  metadata_palette_list[["group"]] <- c(
    metadata_palette_list[["group"]], n[["group"]]
  )
}
metadata_palette_list[["library"]] <- setNames("#969696", c("WT"))
for (i in seq(1, length(subunit_pal_names))) {
  n <- read_counts_df %>%
    filter(subunit == subunit_pal_names[[i]]) %>%
    distinct(library) %>%
    colour_metadata(brewer_palette_name = names(subunit_pal_names)[i])
  metadata_palette_list[["library"]] <- c(
    metadata_palette_list[["library"]], n[["library"]]
  )
}

```

# Ty1 insertion quantification at tRNA genes

```{r load-trna-locations}
trna_df <- load_trna_region_data_frame(p.bt.trna_bed_path)

trna_df <- trna_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    trna.type = gsub(pattern = '^(t.).*',
                     replacement = '\\1',
                     x = trna.name)
  )
```

Loaded `r nrow(trna_df)` tRNA gene locations.

```{r write-trna-gene-summary}
writexl::write_xlsx(
  x = list(
    "gene positions" = trna_df,
    "summary" = trna_df %>% 
      group_by(trna.type) %>% 
      tally(name = "gene.count") %>% 
      arrange(desc(gene.count))
  ),
  path = file.path(params$output_dir, "trna_gene_summary.xlsx")
)
```


```{r load-coverage-data}
# TEST:

bt.cov_df <- purrr::imap(
  .x = setNames(
    file.path(p.bt.trna_cov_dir, p.bt.input_trna_coverage_file_names),
    names(p.bt.input_trna_coverage_file_names)),

missing <- trna_df %>% 
  dplyr::filter(! trna.name %in% unique(dplyr::pull(bt.cov_df, trna.name)))

if (nrow(missing) > 0) {

          sep = "")

}
```

```{r transform-data}
bt.cov_df <- normalise_sequencing_library_coverage(
  df = bt.cov_df,
  read_counts = read_counts_df,
  read_norm_type = "raw_f1"
)

libs_missing <- filter(bt.cov_df, is.na(coverage.norm)) %>% 
  distinct(library) %>% 
  pull(library)

if (length(libs_missing) >= 1) {
  stop(
    paste("Unable to calculate coverage for libraries",
          paste(libs_missing, collapse = ", "))
  )
}

```

## Butterfly plot

```{r plot-butterfly, fig.cap = "Butterfly plot showing the normalised sequencing coverage -- a proxy for the number of Ty1 insertions -- upstream and downstream of a tRNA gene. Sequencing coverage was normalised by the number of reads sequenced for each library. tRNA genes encoded on the mitochondrial chromosome were omitted."}
nucleosome_position_df <- data.frame(
  x = c(860, 685, 510, 335, 160),
  y = 0
)

p.span <- 0.08  # Controls the amount of smoothing for the default loess smoother
# (0.75 by default). Values between 0.08 and 0.05 retain the double-peak.
p.level <- 0.99  # Level of confidence interval to use (0.95 by default).
bt.cov_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subunit, group, library, proximity, strand, rel.position) %>%
  summarise(
    coverage.norm = sum(coverage.norm),
    .groups = "keep"
  ) %>% 
  plot_butterfly(annot_df = nucleosome_position_df,
                 trna_feat_df = trna_df,
                 colour_by = library,
                 colour_palette = metadata_palette_list[["library"]],
                 span = p.span,
                 level = p.level,
                 .smooth_se = TRUE,
                 .annot_size = 4)
```

The smoothing function (LOESS) greatly effects the shape and of coverage distributions in the butterfly plot. The LOESS function (default) had the best fit, with the formula `y ~ x`.
The `span` and `length` parameters used by `geom_smooth` also impacted the fit of the model. In order to preserve the double peak of Ty1 insertion per nucleosome the span was set to `r p.span` and level was set to `r p.level`.

## Insertion rate differences between strands

### Box-and-whisker plot

Next, we wanted to learn whether there was a difference in Ty1 insertion between the positive and negative strands.

```{r strand-wise-box-and-whisker, fig.cap="Comparison of normalised read depths between the positive and negative strands.", fig.height=6, fig.width=8}

bt.strand_diff_df <- bt.cov_df %>%
  group_by(group, library, trna.name, proximity, strand, subunit, strain.type, sugar) %>%
  mutate(strand = ifelse(strand == '+',
                         "positive",
                         "negative")) %>% 
  reframe(coverage.sum = sum(coverage.norm))

bt.strand_diff_df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = strand, y = coverage.sum, colour = proximity)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(subunit),
             cols = vars(strain.type))+ 
  labs(x = "DNA strand",
       y = "Normalised read depth") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "")) +
  theme_bw()
```

There is no significant difference between the two strands. Coverage upstream of tRNA genes is clearly greater than downstream.

### Strand insertion at each tRNA gene

```{r strand-difference-box-and-whisker, fig.cap="Coverage difference values were calculated by subtracting the coverage of the negative strand from the coverage of the positive strand for each tRNA gene. Only positions upstream of the tRNA genes were used."}

bt.strand_diff_df %>% 
  filter(proximity == "upstream",
         subunit != "Other") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "strand",
              values_from = "coverage.sum",
              values_fill = 0) %>% 
  mutate(strand_diff = positive - negative) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(aes(x = group,
                      y = strand_diff,
                      colour = interaction(strain.type, sugar, sep = '+'))) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot() +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = vars(subunit),
                      scales = "free_y",
                      space = "free") +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  ggplot2::guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Treatment")) +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "",
    y = "",
    # y = "Difference between positive and negative\nstrand coverage at tRNA genes"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()

```

## Mutant versus wild-type

Ty1 retrotransposons use the RNA polymerase machinery to insert into the genome upstream of the genes transcribed by the respective RNA polymerase enzyme -- in this case, RNA polymerase III. The RNA polymerase III subunits  [RPC160](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/RPC160), [RPC53](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000002309) and [RPC34](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/RPC34) are all necessary for transcription. To test which subunits associate with Ty1 retrotransposon's insertion machinery, each of the three subunit-encoding genes were systematically mutated and its consequent impact on insertion was analysed. A baseline of no insertion was inferred from *S. cerevisae* grown on dextrose.


```{r mutant-vs-wildtype-insertion-box-plot, fig.cap="Comparison of normalised coverage between the mutant and wild-type strains for each subunit group. For this box-plot, coverage values for only the upstream regions were used as insertion in the downstream was always less. Coverage across all tRNA genes on both strands was summed, yielding 275 data points for each library: one for each tRNA gene.", fig.height=5}
bt.cov_df %>% 
  filter(proximity == "upstream",
         subunit != "Other") %>% 
  group_by(strain.type, sugar, subunit, trna.name, group) %>% 
  reframe(coverage.sum = sum(coverage.norm)) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = group,
                               y = coverage.sum,
                               colour = interaction(strain.type, sugar, sep = '+'))) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot() +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(~ subunit,
                      scales = "free_x",
                      space = "free") +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  ggplot2::guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Treatment")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "",
                y = "Normalized 5'-most nucleotide coverage") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

```

```{r mutant-vs-wt-distribution, fig.cap="Distributions of mutant and wild-type coverage around tRNA genes. Dashed vertical lines indicate the mean coverage values for each group. Coverage was summed for each tRNA gene and library (__a__), and RNA polymerase II subunit (__b__).", fig.height=5, fig.width=13}
dist_plot.a <- bt.cov_df %>% 
  group_by(strain.type, trna.name, library) %>% 
  summarise(coverage.sum = sum(coverage.norm),
            .groups = "keep") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = coverage.sum,
             fill = strain.type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Normalized 5'-most nucleotide coverage",
                y = "") +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = "none") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )

dist_plot.b <- bt.cov_df %>% 
  group_by(strain.type, trna.name, library, subunit) %>% 
  summarise(coverage.sum = sum(coverage.norm),
            .groups = "keep") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log(coverage.sum),
             fill = strain.type,
             colour = strain.type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(~subunit) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Log-normalized 5'-most nucleotide coverage",
                y = "") +
  stat_summary(aes(xintercept = after_stat(x),
                   y = 0),
               fun = mean, 
               geom = "vline", 
               orientation = "y",
               linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = guide_legend(title = ""),
                  colour = "none") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank()
  )

cowplot::plot_grid(dist_plot.a, dist_plot.b,
                   align = "hv",
                   labels = "auto",
                   axis = "tb",
                   rel_heights = c(1,1),
                   rel_widths = c(1, 3))
```

```{r mutant-vs-wt-t-test, tab.cap="Result of a Welch's two-sided t-test under the null hypothesis that there is no difference between the tRNA coverages of mutant and wild-type strains."}

bt.cov_t_test_res_table <- bt.cov_df %>%
  filter(sugar == "Galactose",
         subunit != "Other",
         proximity == "upstream") %>%
  group_by(strain.type, trna.name, library, subunit, group) %>%
  summarise(coverage.sum = sum(coverage.norm),
            .groups = "keep") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subunit) %>%
  tidyr::nest() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ttest = purrr::map(data,
                       subunit_wise_t_test_helper,
                       paired = FALSE,
                       conf.level = 0.99,
                       alternative = "two.sided",
                       values_col = "coverage.sum")
  ) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(ttest) %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(c("subunit", "group", "statistic", "p.value", "wt.mean", "mut.mean"))) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    digits = Inf,
    col.names = c("Subunit", "Library", "T-test statistic", "p-value", "WT mean", "Mutant mean")
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_minimal()

bt.cov_t_test_res_table
kableExtra::save_kable(
  bt.cov_t_test_res_table,
  file = file.path(params$output_dir, "t-test_tRNA_coverage_table.pdf")
)

```

# Ty1 insertions at RNA Polymerase II transcribed genes

```{r load-rna-pol-ii-table, eval=TRUE}
rpii.cov_columns <- c("library", "seqid", "position", "strand", "feature", "coverage")
rpii.cov_df <- readr::read_tsv(file=p.rpii.cov_file,
                               col_names = rpii.cov_columns) %>% 
  mutate(library = gsub(pattern = "[[:punct:]]",
                        replacement = '-',
                        x = library)) %>% 
  filter(! library %in% p.libs_for_filtering) %>%
  normalise_sequencing_library_coverage(read_counts = read_counts_df,
                                        read_norm_type = "raw") %>% 
  dplyr::rename(
    "coverage.raw" = coverage,
    "coverage" = coverage.norm
  )

rpii.gene_df <- readr::read_tsv(file=p.rpii.feature_bed_file,
                               col_names = c("seqid", "start", "stop", "feature", "strand")) %>% 
  group_by(feature) %>% 
  mutate(id = row_number()) %>% 
  filter(id == 2) %>% # Grab just the true coordinates of the gene. 1 & 3 correspond to buffer regions.
  select(feature, start, stop) %>% 
  mutate(length = stop - start)
```

```{r summarise-rpii-coverages}
rpii_rel_pos_df <- rpii.cov_df %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(rpii.gene_df,
                   by = "feature") %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    subunit != "Other",
    sugar == "Galactose"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    rel_position = case_when(
      (position < start) & (strand == "-") ~ (position - start) * -1,
      (position < start & strand == "+") ~ position - start,
      (position > stop & strand == "+") ~ position + 100 - stop,
      (position > stop & strand == "-") ~ (position + 100 - stop) * -1,
      .default = round(100 * (position - start) / length, 1)
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(rel_position >= -600 & rel_position <= 600) %>% 
  group_by(library, subunit, rel_position) %>% 
  reframe(
    coverage = sum(coverage),
    coverage.raw = sum(coverage.raw)
  )

rpii_rel_pos_df %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    rel_position = case_when(
      rel_position < 0 ~ "upstream",
      rel_position > 100 ~ "downstream",
      .default = "within Pol II gene"
    )
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(library, subunit, rel_position) %>% 
  dplyr::reframe(
    coverage = sum(coverage),
    coverage.raw = sum(coverage.raw)
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(
    "Library" = library,
    "Subunit" = subunit,
    "Relative position" = rel_position,
    "Coverage" = coverage,
    "Reads mapped" = coverage.raw
  ) %>% 
writexl::write_xlsx(
  path = file.path(params$output_dir, "rpii_rel_pos_cov.xlsx"),
)

rpii_gene_cov_table <- rpii_rel_pos_df %>% 
  group_by(library, subunit) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(
    "insertionCount" = n(),
    "readCount" = sum(coverage.raw),
    "coverageSum" = round(sum(coverage), 4),
    "coverageMean" = round(mean(coverage), 9),
    # features_gt_1 = n_distinct(feature[coverage.raw > 1]),
    # # Count unique features where coverage.raw > 10
    # features_gt_2 = n_distinct(feature[coverage.raw > 2]),
    # # Count unique features where coverage.raw > 100
    # features_gt_10 = n_distinct(feature[coverage.raw > 10]),
    # Add a column for the total number of unique features in the library (optional, but useful)
    # total_unique_features = n_distinct(feature),
    .groups = "keep"
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  arrange(subunit, insertionCount) %>% 
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Library",
      "Subunit",
      "Insertion Position Count",
      "Read Count",
      "Coverage Sum",
      "Coverage Mean"
      # "No. genes with >1 insertion",
      # "No. genes with >2 insertions",
      # "No. genes with >10 insertions"
    ),
    digits = 9
  ) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_minimal()

rpii_gene_cov_table
kableExtra::save_kable(
  rpii_gene_cov_table,
  file = file.path(params$output_dir, "RNA_Pol_II_gene_coverage_summary.pdf")
)

```

rpii.short_cov_df <- rpii.cov_df %>%

rpii.short_cov_df %>%

rpii_short_orf_reads <- rpii.short_cov_df %>%

(100 * rpii_short_orf_reads) / rpii.cov_df %>% pull(coverage.raw) %>% sum()

rpii.short_cov_df %>%
  group_by(feature, library) %>% 
  reframe(total = sum(coverage.raw)) %>% 
  summary()

```

```{r test-rna-pol-ii-table, eval=FALSE}
row_count <- 6000

replicate_items <- function(items, total_count) {
  is.wholenumber <- function(n)
    return(round(n) == n)

  frac <- total_count / length(items)
  if (!is.wholenumber(frac))
    stop(
      paste("total_count is not divisible by number of items:", frac)
    )
  unlist(lapply(items, rep.int, frac))
}

rpii.cov_df <- data.frame(
  library = replicate_items(c('lib_abc'), row_count),
  seqid = replicate_items(c('chr1'), row_count),
  strand = replicate_items(c('+'), row_count),
  rel_position = seq.int(from = 0, length.out = row_count, by = 2),
  coverage = round(rnorm(row_count, mean = 3, sd = 3)),
  feature = replicate_items(c('gene1', 'gene2', 'gene3'), row_count)
) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    feature = gsub(pattern = "^gene-", replacement = "", x = feature)
  )

rpii.gene_df <- data.frame(
  feature = c('gene1', 'gene2', 'gene3'),
  start = c(0, 1000, 2000),
  stop = c(1000, 2000, 3000),
  length = c(1000, 1000, 1000)
)

rpii.nucleosome_df <- readxl::read_xlsx(
  path = "data/input/13059_2018_1398_MOESM2_ESM.xlsx"
) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    "Nucleosome_up" = "+1 nucleosome",
    "Nucleosome_down" = "-1 nucleosome"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::select(ORF, Chr, TSS, TTS, Nucleosome_up, Nucleosome_down)
  

```

```{r plot-absolute-position-coverage, fig.cap="Position-wise coverages across genes transcribed by RNA Polymerase II. Coverage values represent summed deduplicated alignment counts at each position, normalised by the sequencing library's total read counts. Ranges include 500 bp upstream and downstream (-500 and 500, respectively), and include the first and last 500 bp of an ORF. 3,707 of 5,199 annotated ORFs longer than 1,000 bp and with at least one read alignment were included."}

rpii.cov_df %>%
  prep_position_wise_feature_coverage_df(rpii.gene_df,
                                         min_gene_coverage = 0,
                                         min_gene_read_count = 1,
                                         add_zero_coverage_positions = FALSE,
                                         summarise_by_position = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::rename("coverage" = "coverage.sum") %>% 
  extract_metadata_from_library_names() %>%
  filter(
    subunit %in% c("RPC34", "RPC53", "RPC160"),
    sugar == "Galactose"
  ) %>%
  plot_position_coverage(
    x_var = rel_position,
    plot_type = "smooth",
    free_y_scale = TRUE,
    palette_vals = metadata_palette_list[["library"]],
    text_gap_size = 120,
    loess_span = 0.05,
    label_y_position = 9E-6  # 3E-7 when positions with zero reads mapped are included
  )

```

```{r plot-relative-position-coverage, fig.cap="Normalised coverage values across the lengths of genes transcribed by RNA polymerase II, relative to their predicted ORF length. Coverage values were summed across relative ORF position (i.e., upstream, percentage through the ORF, or downstream)."}
get_percentage_display_positions <- function(df) {
  df %>% 
    mutate(
    rel_position = case_when(
      (position < start) & (strand == "-") ~ (position - start) * -1,
      (position < start & strand == "+") ~ position - start,
      (position > stop & strand == "+") ~ position + 100 - stop,
      (position > stop & strand == "-") ~ (position + 100 - stop) * -1,
      (start <= position & position <= stop & strand == "+") ~ round(100 * (position - start) / length, 1),
       (start <= position & position <= stop & strand == "-") ~ round(100 * (stop - position) / length, 1),
      .default = NA
    ),
    display_position = case_when(
      # 1. Upstream (0 to 1)
      rel_position <= 0 ~ rel_position / 500,

      # 3. Downstream (2 to 3)
      rel_position >= 100 ~ 2 + (rel_position - 601) / 500,
      
      # 2. Gene Body (1 to 2) - This section must be scaled to occupy a space of 1
      .default = rel_position / 100,

    )
  ) %>% 
    return()
}

```{r rna-pol-ii-subunit-coverage-t-test, tab.cap="P-values from Kruskal-Wallis tests comparing normalised coverage values between all mutant strains to wild-type for each subunit."}

test_coverage_by_group <- function(df) {
  groups <- unique(df$group)
  # Kruskal-Wallis test for >2 groups
  res <- kruskal.test(coverage ~ group, data = df)
  return(list(test = "Kruskal-Wallis", p.value = res$p.value))
}

rpii.gene_cov_df <- rpii.cov_df %>% 
  left_join(rpii.gene_df,
            by = "feature") %>% 
  filter(
    sugar == "Galactose",
    subunit != "Other",
    length > 500
  ) %>%
  select(subunit, strain.type, group, feature, coverage)

results <- lapply(unique(rpii.gene_cov_df[["subunit"]]), function(sub) {
  df_sub <- rpii.gene_cov_df %>%
    filter(subunit == sub)
  res <- test_coverage_by_group(df_sub)
  data.frame(subunit = sub,
             test = res$test,
             p.value = res$p.value)
})

# Print results
rpii.subunit_cov_test_kable <- do.call(rbind, results) %>%
  select(all_of(c("subunit", "p.value"))) %>% 
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Subunit", "p-value")) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_minimal()

rpii.subunit_cov_test_kable
kableExtra::save_kable(
  rpii.subunit_cov_test_kable,
  file = file.path(params$output_dir, "RNA_Pol_II_gene_coverage_subunit_test_results.pdf"))
```

```{r rna-pol-ii-strain-coverage-t-test, tab.cap="Results from two-sided Student's t-Tests comparing normalised gene coverages between mutant strains and wild-type (WT). Mean WT and mutant values represent the mean normalised coverage values across all predicted ORFs in the genome."}
rpii.strain_cov_test_kable <- rpii.gene_cov_df %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(subunit) %>%
  tidyr::nest() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ttest = purrr::map(data,
                       subunit_wise_t_test_helper,
                       paired = FALSE,
                       conf.level = 0.99,
                       alternative = "two.sided",
                       values_col = "coverage")
  ) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(ttest) %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(c("subunit", "group", "statistic", "p.value", "wt.mean", "mut.mean"))) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    digits = Inf,
    col.names = c("Subunit", "Library", "T-test statistic", "p-value", "WT mean", "Mutant mean")
  ) %>%

rpii.strain_cov_test_kable
kableExtra::save_kable(

# Genome-wide Ty1 insertion site analysis

As part of the Ty1 insertion site experiments, genes in the knock-out mutants were rescued by copies on a plasmid. Since these were not located on the chromosome, however, we wanted to remove their contributions to coverage values. These regions are defined in the following table.

```{r calc-trna-coverage-for-mutant-and-wt}

# Currently hard-coded for tRNA features
calculate_feature_coverage_between_mutant_and_wt <- function(df) {
  cols <- c(
    "subunit",
    "strain.type",
    "group",
    "chr",
    "strand",
    "end",
    "trna.name",
    "proximity",
    "mean_cov.norm"
  )
  
  df.wt <- df %>% 
    dplyr::filter(strain.type == "Wild-type") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(strain.type = "WT") %>%
    dplyr::select(tidyselect::all_of(cols)) %>% 
    dplyr::distinct() %>% 
    pivot_wider(names_from = "strain.type",
                values_from = "mean_cov.norm")
  
  df %>%
    dplyr::filter(strain.type == "Mutant") %>% 
    dplyr::select(tidyselect::all_of(cols)) %>% 
    dplyr::distinct() %>% 
    pivot_wider(names_from = "strain.type",
                values_from = "mean_cov.norm") %>% 
    left_join(df.wt,
              by = c("subunit", "chr", "strand", "end", "trna.name", "proximity"),
              suffix = c('', '.wt')) %>%
    group_by(subunit, group, trna.name, proximity) %>% 
    summarise(
      wt.sum = sum(WT),
      wt.mean = mean(WT),
      mut.sum = sum(Mutant),
      mut.mean = mean(Mutant),
      .groups = "keep"
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>% 
    mutate(diff.abs = abs(mut.mean - wt.mean)) %>% 
    return()
}

trna_cov_df.mut_vs_wt <- hm.full_cov_df %>%
  filter(
    grepl(pattern = 'tRNA', x = feature.name),
    ! library %in% p.libs_for_filtering
  ) %>%
  filter(
    sugar == "Galactose",
    subunit != "Other"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(trna_df %>% 
                     select(trna.name, chr, end, strand),
                   by = c("chr", "end", "strand")) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(trna_df %>% 
                     select(trna.name, chr, start, strand),
                   by = c("chr", "end" = "start", "strand"),
                   suffix = c('', '.up')) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(trna_df %>% 
                     select(trna.name, chr, end, strand),
                   by = c("chr", "start" = "end", "strand"),
                   suffix = c('', '.down')) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    trna.name = coalesce(trna.name, trna.name.up, trna.name.down),
    trna.name = gsub(pattern = '^(t.).*',
                     replacement = '\\1',
                     x = trna.name),
    proximity = case_when(
      feature.name == "tRNA" ~ "gene",
      feature.name == "tRNA upstream" ~ "upstream",
      feature.name == "tRNA downstream" ~ "downstream",
      .default = NA
    )
  ) %>%
  summarise_coverage_by_feature(subunit, strain.type, group, chr, end, strand, trna.name, proximity) %>%
  dplyr::filter(trna.name != "tX") %>% 
  calculate_feature_coverage_between_mutant_and_wt()

```{r trna-coverage-t-test, tab.cap=paste("Welch's two-sample t-test results comparing tRNA coverage (within the gene) between mutants and wild-type. The tRNAs", paste(outlier_trna_type_list, collapse=', '), "were tested as they were observed to be outliers from the scatterplot figure.")}
trna_cov_df <- hm.full_cov_df %>%
  filter(
    feature.name == 'tRNA',
    ! library %in% p.libs_for_filtering,
    sugar == "Galactose",
    subunit != "Other"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(trna_df %>% 
                     select(all_of(c("trna.name", "trna.type", "chr", "end", "strand"))),
                   by = c("chr", "end", "strand")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    coverage.sum = coverage.pbp.norm
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subunit, strain.type, group, trna.type) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(trna_obs = n()) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    trna.type %in% outlier_trna_type_list,
    trna_obs > 3
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(c("subunit", "sugar", "strain.type", "group", "trna.name", "trna.type", "coverage.sum")))

trna_cov_stats_df <- trna_cov_df %>%
  group_by(subunit, group, trna.type) %>%
  dplyr::reframe(
    mean = mean(coverage.sum),
    var = var(coverage.sum)
  )

trna_t_test_res_df <- trna_cov_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subunit, trna.type) %>%
  tidyr::nest() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ttest = purrr::map(data,
                       subunit_wise_t_test_helper,
                       paired = FALSE,
                       conf.level = 0.99,
                       alternative = "two.sided",
                       values_col = "coverage.sum")
  ) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(ttest) %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(c("subunit", "trna.type", "group", "p.value", "wt.mean"))) %>% 
  left_join(trna_cov_stats_df,
            by = c("subunit", "trna.type", "group"))

bold_rows <- which(trna_t_test_res_df$p.value < 0.05)

trna_t_test_res_df %>%
  knitr::kable()

kableExtra::save_kable(
  x = trna_t_test_res_df %>%
    knitr::kable(
      digits = Inf,
      col.names = c("Subunit", "tRNA", "Library", "p-value", "WT mean", "Mutant mean", "Mutant variance")
    ) %>% 
    kableExtra::row_spec(bold_rows, bold = TRUE) %>% 
    kableExtra::kable_minimal(),
  file = file.path(params$output_dir, "t-test_tRNA_gene_coverage_table.pdf")
)

```

```{r least-targeted-trna-genes, tab.cap="The mean and sum normalised read coverage values upstream of and in tRNA genes for each sequencing library. Genes are ordered by the mean and sum coverage values across all libraries."}
trna_cov_df.mut_vs_wt %>%
  filter(proximity != "downstream") %>%

    c("trna.name", "subunit", "group", "proximity", "mut.sum", "mut.mean")

  file = file.path(params$output_dir, "all_tRNA_coverage_table.pdf")
)

# Appendix

## Ty1 insertion quantification at tRNA genes

```{r nucleosome-coverage-plot}
match_trna_by_position <- function(df1, df2) {
  # df1: Data frame with at least a 'position' column
  # df2: Data frame with at least 'start', 'end', and 'trna.name' columns
  # Returns: df1 with a new column 'matched_trna.name' containing the trna.name from df2 if a match is found, NA otherwise

  # Vector to hold matched trna.names
  matched_names <- vector("character", nrow(df1))
  
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(df1))) {
    pos <- df1$position[i]
    chr <- df1$chr[i]
    
    # Find matching trna in df2 where position is within 1000 of start and end
    match_idx <- which((chr == df2$chr) & (pos >= df2$start - 1000) & (pos <= df2$end + 1000))
    
    if (length(match_idx) > 0) {
      # If multiple matches, choose the first one
      matched_names[i] <- as.character(df2$trna.name[match_idx[1]])
    } else {
      matched_names[i] <- NA
    }
  }
  
  # Add matched_trna.name to df1
  df1$trna.name <- matched_names
  return(df1)
}

nuc_pos_df <- read.table(p.bt.npc_file,
                         header=FALSE,
                         col.names = c("chr", "position", "NPC", "noiseRatio"))
nuc_pos_df %>%
  filter(
    noiseRatio > 1,
    # NPC > 1
  ) %>%
  match_trna_by_position(trna_df) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(trna.name)) %>% 
  dplyr::right_join(trna_df,
                    by = c("chr", "trna.name")) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    rel_position = position - start,
    rel_position = case_when(
      strand == '-' ~ (rel_position * -1),
      .default = rel_position
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(rel_position) %>% 
  mutate(
    npc.mean = mean(NPC),
    npc.sum = sum(NPC)
  ) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = rel_position, y = npc.mean)) +
  geom_smooth(
    # method = "loess",
    # formula = y ~ x,
    # span = 0.1,
    # level = p.level,
    se = FALSE
  )
```

### Mean TPM and coverage relationship

The following figure is to determine how the choice between TPM and coverage influences the results and potentially the interpretation.

```{r cov-tpm-scatter-plot, fig.cap="Mean coverage and TPM values are linearly correlated, and the slope of the relationship is explained by the library.", fig.height=4, fig.width=10}
hm.cov_df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_cov, y = mean_tpm, colour = library)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_bw()
```

The figure above shows that there is less differentiation between the different libraries when using TPM values (y-axis) compared to using coverage values (x-axis). Whether this reflects true signal or a lack of normalization in calculating coverage values is not clear.

## Coverage at genes transcribed by RNA Polymerase II

```{r separate-rna-pol-ii-gene-insertions, fig.height=6, fig.width=11, fig.cap="Position-wise normalised coverage values for genes transcribed by RNA Polymerase II."}
target_subunits <- c("RPC34", "RPC160")

rpii.cov_prepped_df <- rpii.cov_df %>%
  prep_position_wise_feature_coverage_df(
    rpii.gene_df,
    min_gene_coverage = 0,
    min_gene_read_count = 1,
    add_zero_coverage_positions = FALSE,
    summarise_by_position = TRUE
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename("coverage" = "coverage.sum") %>% 
  extract_metadata_from_library_names() %>%
  filter(
    subunit %in% target_subunits,
    sugar == "Galactose"
  )

for (subunit_name in target_subunits) {
  for (lib_name in unique(rpii.cov_prepped_df$library)) {
    if (grepl(pattern = "WT", x = lib_name, ignore.case = FALSE)) {
      next()
    }
    if (!grepl(pattern = subunit_name, x = lib_name, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      next()
    }
    plt <- rpii.cov_prepped_df %>% 
      filter(
        (library %in% c(lib_name) | group == "WT"),
        subunit == subunit_name
      ) %>%
      plot_position_coverage(
        plot_type = "smooth",
        free_y_scale = TRUE,
        palette_vals = metadata_palette_list[["library"]],
        text_gap_size = 120,
        loess_span = 0.05,
        label_y_position = 9E-6
      )
    plt <- plt +
      ggplot2::theme(
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_blank()
      )
    plot(plt)
  }
}
```
